newsitem.title: USA: Harriman laid to rest at family estate.
newsitem.headline: Harriman laid to rest at family estate.

text.p: Pamela Harriman, a British-born aristocrat who became a doyenne of Washington society and the U.S. Ambassador to France, was buried on Friday at the family estate of her late husband.
About 60 friends and family attended the private funeral service and burial at the estate, an elegant setting of open fields and wooded hills about 45 miles (75 km) north of New York City.
Harriman's coffin was draped with an American flag, which was presented to her son, Member of Parliament Winston S. Churchill.
She was buried next to the body of her late husband, Averell Harriman, a governor of New York. The burial ceremony was held under a green awning to protect against the snow and rain.
No members of the media were permitted to attend the private ceremony.
Witnesses said there was no eulogy or personalized tribute to Harriman, who was remembered by President Bill Clinton at a memorial serivce in Washington on Thursday as "truly indomitable."
"Today, I am here in no small measure because she was there," he added, recalling her role as a top Democratic party fund-raiser.
Harriman, named U.S. ambassador to France in 1993, died at age 76 last week after suffering a brain hemmorhage after a swim in the Hotel Ritz in Paris.

A reception followed the burial Friday at Arden House, a nationally landmarked mansion that lies at the end of a 3 1/2 mile (5 km) driveway. The house sits atop a hilltop, with dramatic views of a river and two lakes. A cable railway once carried guests and supplies from the estate gates below.
The estate also includes a graveyard with headstones for a number of dogs, a reminder of the days when members of the Harriman family raised hunting dogs.
Harriman's first husband was Randolph Churchill, son of the late British Prime Minister Winston Churchill. She later was married to Leland Hayward, a theatrical producer, and then to Harriman.

After Harriman's death in 1986, she devoted herself to helping rebuild the Democratic Party weakened by years of Republican White House domination. She was legendary for hosting power dinners at her home in Washington's swank Georgetown neighbourhood.
